text: Thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, dehydration likely

detail.problem: The four parts (thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60) are each encoded with a fitting concept, BP < 90/60 correctly as SBP < 90 or DBP < 60, and the conclusion is a probable Dehydration rule referenced by the priority rule. The logic is wrong: the rule uses 'or' across the four, so thirst alone (or dry mouth alone) in a tired patient yields a probable dehydration diagnosis and an Urgent priority. The page lists these as the cluster that together makes dehydration likely (it uses explicit 'or' elsewhere on the same line-set when it means any-of, e.g. 'Difficulty breathing or respiratory rate >= 30', and explicit 'and' in the heart-failure item). The honest reading is a conjunction or at least any2; 'or' over-triggers both the diagnosis and the Urgent level.
